args.text: We propose Loss-Decomposed Gradient Projection (LDGP) for class-incremental continual learning: decouple the training loss into (i) separating new from old classes and (ii) discriminating among new classes, and handle their gradients with different geometry. We maintain per-layer activation subspaces of prior tasks (as in gradient projection memory) and project the separation-loss gradient strictly onto the orthogonal complement of the union of old-task subspaces to prevent boundary drift on past classes. For the within-new-class gradient, we apply a soft, layer-wise trust-region reuse of selected prior task directions to enable positive transfer while still constraining interference; additionally, we meta-learn per-parameter learning rates separately for the two gradient components to adapt the stability–plasticity balance online. This differential projection-and-scaling scheme aims to outperform replay-only decoupling by explicitly shaping gradient flow with task-informed subspace geometry without growing the model or memory.

args.text: Subspace-Targeted Memory Editing and Selection (STEMS) unifies subspace-projection continual learning with replay by maintaining GPM-style layerwise activation bases for past tasks and using them to steer both which examples to store and how to edit them. For each incoming or cached example, we approximate its stability/plasticity influence by decomposing its gradient into components parallel and orthogonal to the stored subspaces, then select or replace buffer items that maximize complementary-subspace coverage while preserving span of old subspaces, and apply GMED-style input edits constrained to increase future loss primarily in the orthogonal complement. During training on a new task, we freeze or scale related layers using TRGP-like trust gating derived from subspace-overlap scores, while projecting updates away from the important bases to avoid interference. This yields replay that explicitly targets capacity for novel directions, improves forward transfer, and reduces forgetting without task IDs and with negligible overhead beyond maintaining compact SVD bases.

result.text: The paper addresses how to obtain good representations for reinforcement learning—especially goal-conditioned tasks—without unstable end-to-end training or ad-hoc auxiliary losses and data augmentations. The key insight is that contrastive representation learning applied to action-labeled trajectories can be interpreted as learning a goal-conditioned value function: the inner product between learned representations of states and goals corresponds exactly to the goal-conditioned value, so contrastive objectives become RL objectives. Building on this equivalence, the authors reinterpret an existing RL algorithm as contrastive learning and introduce a much simpler contrastive-RL method that trains representations via a contrastive loss over (state, action, goal) tuples; empirically this contrastive approach yields higher success rates than prior non-contrastive and offline methods and outperforms baselines on image-based tasks without auxiliary losses or data augmentation.

args.text: We propose Track-Event Semantic Tokenization (TEST) for video multimodal LLMs: a variable-length tokenizer that emits temporally consistent object "track tokens" and compact "event tokens" summarizing motion and inter-object relations, enabling efficient autoregressive reasoning over long videos. TEST clusters frame patches into region tokens and links them across time into tracks with language-assisted aggregation and video-level contrastive alignment, then compresses motion patterns over tracks into event tokens aligned with verb phrases; both token types are trained with joint reconstruction and semantic-separation losses to preserve meaning while reducing redundancy. Integrated into a unified generative interface, TEST aims to cut visual token budgets while improving temporal grounding and natural language video localization via boundary-aware tokenization and auxiliary proposal supervision. It builds on region-level and SOC-style aggregation but extends them into a generative token interface for LLMs that unifies comprehension, localization, and segmentation from language.

result.text: We propose Slot-Adapter UDA, a parameter-efficient framework that injects two lightweight adapters into a frozen image backbone—one static and one dynamic—that operate on object-centric slot tokens for unsupervised video domain adaptation. Slots are obtained via temporal feature-similarity grouping (and optionally hands–object crops); the static adapter learns domain-invariant appearance using background-mixed positives and slot-level supervised/pseudo-label contrast, while the dynamic adapter adds temporal interactions trained with speed perturbations and reversed-time negatives to align motion across domains. We further introduce a slot-transport consistency loss that swaps static slots from source with dynamic slots from target (and vice versa), emulating disentangled transfer without a full generative model. This combines the strengths of contrastive temporal augmentation, object-centric grouping, and disentangled alignment while updating only a small fraction of parameters through adapters.

The key insight is to dynamically and progressively prune redundant tokens per input using a lightweight importance-prediction module inserted at multiple layers, exploiting self-attention so that removed tokens can be masked out without harming differentiable training or hardware efficiency. result.text: The paper addresses the gap between the promise of learned optimizers (L2O) and their practical performance, noting that many L2O models are narrowly applicable and unstable largely due to training challenges. The key insight is that better training procedures—rather than more complex optimizer architectures—can substantially improve L2O performance by mitigating truncation bias and instability and by leveraging guidance from analytic optimizers. Concretely, the authors introduce a progressive training scheme that gradually increases the unroll length to balance truncation bias versus gradient explosion, and they augment learning with off-policy imitation learning that uses analytical optimizer behavior as a reference; these techniques are applied modularly to many existing L2O models and significantly boost their results, allowing even simple early models to outperform recent complicated ones.

args.text: Hierarchical Cross-Decoder Compressed Memory: stack a cross-decoder atop a self-decoder that builds a single global KV cache, but encode that cache with a progressive, head- and layer-adaptive compressor (combining low-rank projections and vector-quantized codes) trained to preserve attention logits under a rate–distortion objective. The cross-decoder maintains only a short uncompressed local KV window and routes each head’s queries either to local KV or to the compressed global memory via a learned gate, enabling early-exit prefilling and sharply reduced memory traffic. Training uses teacher-forced distillation from a decoder-only teacher and auxiliary losses that reconstruct attention maps from original KVs while encouraging cross-layer KV sharing to amortize memory across layers. This unifies single-cache reuse, dynamic KV compression, and global/local separation to target 4–8× KV reduction and 2–4× prefill speedups with minimal quality loss on long-context tasks.

result.text: The paper addresses continual learning for neural networks, specifically how to learn new tasks without forgetting prior ones, without relying on network growth, importance-weighting, or data replay. Its key insight is that interference can be avoided by restricting new-task gradient updates to the subspace orthogonal to directions important for previous tasks, where those important directions are captured via low-dimensional bases of layer-wise activation spaces. The method computes singular value decompositions of post-task activations to extract and store these bases in a compact Gradient Projection Memory (GPM), then projects incoming gradients away from the stored subspaces during training on new tasks, yielding minimal interference and competitive performance on diverse image-classification continual-learning benchmarks.

result.text: The paper addresses improving video object detection by exploiting temporal information more effectively and efficiently to boost both accuracy and speed. Its key insight is that propagating object-level representations (object queries) across frames, rather than dense pixel- or box-level features, can reduce redundant computation on non-key frames and enrich key-frame features with temporal context. The proposed QueryProp framework implements two propagation modes—from sparse key frames to dense non-key frames to avoid reprocessing every frame, and from previous key frames to the current key frame to enhance feature representation—plus an adaptive propagation gate that flexibly selects key frames; experiments on ImageNet VID show competitive accuracy with a favorable accuracy/speed trade-off.

result.text: The paper addresses limitations of sparse mixture-of-expert (MoE) Transformers—such as training instability, token dropping, poor finetuning, and difficulty scaling expert counts—while preserving MoE capacity and low inference cost. The key insight is to replace hard token-to-expert routing with an implicit soft assignment where each expert receives a different weighted combination of all input tokens, enabling fully differentiable routing that avoids dropped tokens and stabilizes training. Methodologically, Soft MoE applies these soft assignments so experts still only process subsets of the combined tokens (keeping inference efficient), integrates this mechanism into Transformer layers for visual recognition, and demonstrates that large Soft MoE models with many experts substantially outperform dense ViTs and prior MoEs while adding minimal inference overhead.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of learning discrete-time stochastic dynamic models with provable stability guarantees, a critical challenge for applications in estimation and control where model instability can be amplified by noise. The key insight is to embed a Lyapunov function directly into the neural network dynamics so that stability is a built-in property rather than an afterthought, enabling almost-sure stability even in stochastic settings. Methodologically, the authors propose two architectures: one that enforces a convex Lyapunov neural network whose structure and training constraints guarantee decrease conditions, and another that enforces stability via an implicit output layer that solves for outputs satisfying Lyapunov-based constraints; both deterministic and stochastic formulations are treated and validated on numerical examples.

result.text: The paper tackles efficient and accurate video salient object detection (VSOD), noting that prior temporal models like LSTM/C3D or vanilla non-local attention either propagate motion slowly or capture motion-agnostic global context with prohibitive cost. Its key insight is that motion cues can be better captured by constraining self-attention to follow the natural continuity of object trajectories, and that organizing such constrained attentions at multiple spatial-temporal scales yields both richer motion modeling and computational savings. Concretely, the authors propose a Constrained Self-Attention (CSA) operation that restricts attention to locally coherent temporal neighborhoods to emphasize motion-consistent interactions, and stack CSA modules in a pyramidal design (PCSA) to handle objects of different sizes and speeds, producing a fast, end-to-end network that outperforms prior methods in accuracy while running at about 110 FPS.

result.text: The paper addresses the difficulty of long-horizon reinforcement learning where performance degrades with task length and effective chaining of lower-level skills requires state abstractions that reflect those skills' capabilities. The key insight is that the value functions of available skills encode scene affordances and thus form a task-relevant, compact abstraction of state that naturally ignores distractors and supports long-horizon planning. The method, Value Function Spaces, constructs a representation by stacking the value functions (or their predictions) of each low-level policy as features for higher-level decision-making, and uses this skill-centric embedding for planning and hierarchical control. Empirical results on maze navigation and robotic manipulation show improved long-horizon performance and better zero-shot generalization compared to baseline model-free and model-based approaches.

result.text: The paper tackles how to enable frozen large language models (LLMs) to both understand and generate non-linguistic modalities (e.g., images, videos) without changing the LLM weights. The key insight is to map pixels to and from the LLM’s own lexical space via a hierarchical "semantic pyramid" of tokens that jointly encode high-level semantics and fine-grained visual detail, so the LLM can reason about and produce visual content using its native vocabulary. Methodologically, SPAE trains an encoder–decoder that converts images into sequences of interpretable lexical tokens aligned with the LLM’s vocabulary and reconstructs images from those tokens using multiscale latent representations, then uses in-context prompting with frozen PaLM 2 and GPT-3.5 to perform and evaluate multimodal understanding and generation tasks. This approach yields the first demonstration of frozen LLM image generation and substantially improves image understanding performance (over 25% relative) under the same frozen-LM setting.

result.text: The paper addresses the overlooked problem of “jailbreaks” in large language models (LLMs) when users employ non-English or multilingual prompts, showing that safety mechanisms tuned for English can fail both unintentionally (users in low-resource languages inadvertently eliciting harmful outputs) and intentionally (malicious actors combining multilingual prompts with attack instructions). The key insight is that language resource availability critically affects vulnerability—low-resource languages produce unsafe content at much higher rates—and that multilingual prompts can significantly amplify the effectiveness of jailbreak attempts, yielding alarmingly high unsafe-output rates for models like ChatGPT and GPT-4. To mitigate this, the authors introduce Self-Defense, an automated framework that generates multilingual adversarial training data for safety fine-tuning, and demonstrate that fine-tuning ChatGPT on this synthetic multilingual dataset substantially reduces unsafe generation across languages.

The canonicalizer is a small LM (or constrained decoding routine) trained to invert common obfuscations, including cipher-character emissions used to evade output filters, and to abstain when semantic confidence is low, with a backoff to multi-pass paraphrase-by-consensus across models. By mapping obfuscated outputs back into standard natural language before detection, CRD directly targets cipher- and glyph-based evasion and can be evaluated as a drop-in defense on JailbreakBench and JAMBench; we hypothesize large reductions in false negatives on cipher-encoded harms with minimal false-positive increase.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of end-to-end weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) from image-level labels, where existing methods produce low-quality pseudo-labels due to incomplete semantic cues. The key insight is that a network can distill richer, complementary semantic information from its own feature correspondences—using self-derived pixel/region affinities as a supervision signal—to refine its predictions without external labels. The proposed Self Correspondence Distillation (SCD) framework trains the model to match its outputs to correspondence-based targets and is combined with a Variation-aware Refine Module that enforces local consistency by computing pixel-level variation, all implemented efficiently in a Transformer-based TSCD architecture. Experiments on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 show that this self-distillation plus variation-aware refinement yields substantially better pseudo-labels and segmentation performance than prior end-to-end WSSS methods.

result.text: The paper addresses the gap between worst-case bounds and practical performance for random-projection matrix sketching used in dimensionality reduction, low-rank approximation, and randomized Newton-type optimization. Its key insight is that modern spectral random-matrix tools let one derive precise, provable expressions for the expected projection (sketch) operator—expressions that depend on the data's spectrum and capture lower-order effects and constant factors that worst-case analyses miss. The method develops novel spectral-analytic techniques to compute these expected projection matrices for common sketches (Gaussian, Rademacher, etc.), then uses those expressions to predict and analyze the performance of low-rank approximation and iterative stochastic optimization procedures in terms of the data's eigenstructure. Empirical validation shows the derived formulas closely match observed behavior across tasks and sketch types, enabling much tighter, data-dependent performance characterization.

result.text: Subspace-Targeted Memory Editing and Selection (STEMS) unifies subspace-projection continual learning with replay by maintaining GPM-style layerwise activation bases for past tasks and using them to steer both which examples to store and how to edit them. For each incoming or cached example, we approximate its stability/plasticity influence by decomposing its gradient into components parallel and orthogonal to the stored subspaces, then select or replace buffer items that maximize complementary-subspace coverage while preserving span of old subspaces, and apply GMED-style input edits constrained to increase future loss primarily in the orthogonal complement. During training on a new task, we freeze or scale related layers using TRGP-like trust gating derived from subspace-overlap scores, while projecting updates away from the important bases to avoid interference. This yields replay that explicitly targets capacity for novel directions, improves forward transfer, and reduces forgetting without task IDs and with negligible overhead beyond maintaining compact SVD bases.

result.text: We propose TrajProp, a flow-conditioned, trajectory-constrained object-query propagation for real-time video object detection. Building on query propagation and deformable attention, each object query predicts a 2D velocity and uncertainty that generate dynamic reference points and restrict cross-frame sampling to a motion-consistent tube, concentrating aggregation where the object actually moves and reducing cost. To handle occlusions, we add a lightweight depth-order head and an amodal memory inspired by flow-conditioned object-centric layers: the model freezes visual updates when occlusion probability is high while maintaining pose via flow, resuming feature updates upon reappearance. Coupled with adaptive frame selection, this trajectory- and occlusion-aware propagation boosts accuracy on fast motion and heavy-occlusion clips at similar compute to keyframe baselines.

args.text: I propose Hashed-Quantized Global Memory (HQGM) for long-context LLM inference: a two-stage decoder where a self-decoder updates a bounded, per-head memory of quantized K/V slots, and a cross-decoder attends only to those slots plus a short local window. Slots are formed by vector-quantizing or LSH-routing keys online and maintaining per-slot exponential-moving-average K/V sketches (optionally low-rank), so attention cost and KV footprint scale with the number of slots rather than sequence length. Training uses consistency distillation to match dense decoder-only outputs and head-wise, ratio-scheduled compression so the model learns which heads require finer slot granularity; at inference this enables early-exit prefilling and sublinear memory without quality loss. result.text: The paper addresses the mismatch in offline return-conditioned supervised learning (RCSL) where deterministic trajectory modeling ignores stochastic transitions and the discrepancy between sampled trajectory returns and expected returns. The proposed Critic-Guided Decision Transformer (CGDT) augments a Decision Transformer with a critic that predicts long-term returns and guides target-return conditioning so that specified returns align with expected returns of actions, combining value-based predictability with sequence-modeling of trajectories. args.text: We propose TEV-Token, a task-conditioned hierarchical video tokenizer that converts a clip into a variable-length sequence of discrete tokens consisting of (a) entity-tracklet tokens summarizing spatio-temporal object trajectories and attributes, and (b) event-interaction tokens capturing actions and relations between entities, connected via explicit pointer/link tokens. We propose Adversarial Obfuscation Game (AOG), a two-player min–max training loop that learns a robust moderation layer by co-optimizing against a strong obfuscator. The obfuscator is a small LM that transforms harmful texts into filter-evasive outputs via cipher-character substitution, leetspeak/homoglyphs, spacing/noise, and sparse token-level perturbations inspired by ADC, while the defender is a canonicalizer–detector that deciphers/normalizes then applies a PARDEN-style repeat-consistency check before flagging. We propose SafeSketch-GN-Comp: a stabilized, adaptive-sketch Gauss–Newton method for stochastic multi-level compositional optimization that augments sketched inner Jacobians with a provable descent safeguard. args.text: Cross-Layer Codebook Caching shares a single quantized K/V memory across adjacent transformer layers: each layer projects its keys into a common codebook space and writes aggregated per-codeword K/V statistics that are reused by its neighbors instead of storing full per-layer KV caches. Queries read from this shared memory via per-layer adapters, with optional sparse value residuals for hard tokens, so per-token attention cost scales with codebook size rather than sequence length while amortizing KV across depth. A lightweight controller applies dynamic per-head compression schedules to choose raw, quantized, or residual-augmented paths, further shrinking memory and IO. This combines cross-layer reuse with vector-quantized attention caches and online compression to target 2–4× additional KV reduction over cross-layer attention while maintaining quality.

result.text: The paper tackles catastrophic forgetting in continual learning by enabling positive forward transfer from related past tasks while avoiding interference with them. The key insight is to identify a layer-wise "trust region" of previously learned tasks that are most relevant to a new task using the norm of the gradient projection onto subspaces spanned by task inputs, and then selectively reuse their frozen weights via a learned layer-wise scaling. The method, Trust Region Gradient Projection (TRGP), performs a single-shot selection of related tasks per layer, freezes those task weights but applies scaled weight projection and jointly optimizes scaling matrices while updating the model only along directions orthogonal to old-task subspaces, thereby promoting transfer without forgetting. Empirically, TRGP yields significant improvements over prior state-of-the-art continual learning approaches.

result.text: The paper tackles accurate and efficient object detection in 360° imagery, where traditional equirectangular or perspective-based bounding box and IoU measures are either biased or slow for real-world panoramic scenes. Its key insight is that operating directly on the sphere with spherical bounding boxes and a spherical IoU (SphIoU) yields more geometrically faithful and computationally effective criteria than projecting to ERP or PSP alone. The paper reframes reinforcement learning as a sequence modeling problem and addresses the challenge of producing high-return action sequences without relying on value-function estimation or policy-gradient optimization. The key insight is that a causally masked Transformer can be conditioned on past states, past actions, and a target return to autoregressively generate future actions that achieve that return, leveraging the scalability and simplicity of large-scale sequence models. Their method, Decision Transformer, concatenates returns-to-go, states, and actions into tokens and trains a Transformer to predict the next action given this conditioned trajectory; at test time the model autoregressively samples actions conditioned on a desired return to control an agent. Across offline benchmarks (Atari, OpenAI Gym, Key-to-Door) this simple conditional sequence-modeling approach matches or exceeds prior model-free offline RL baselines.

result.text: The paper investigates whether safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) holds when users communicate in non-natural languages (ciphers), addressing the risk that current defenses—trained primarily on natural language—may be bypassed. The key insight is that LLMs can understand and respond to ciphered prompts, and in fact exhibit a latent "secret cipher" behavior that can be triggered via role play and enciphered demonstrations, enabling stealthy jailbreaks even against strong models like GPT-4. The authors introduce CipherChat, a framework that sends system-role descriptions and few-shot enciphered examples to LLMs to systematically evaluate 11 safety domains across English and Chinese, showing that many human-designed ciphers and the proposed SelfCipher can nearly completely bypass GPT-4’s safety in several domains. Their results reveal a pressing need to extend alignment methods beyond natural languages and provide code and data for reproducibility.

result.text: The paper tackles accurate and efficient object detection in 360° imagery, where traditional equirectangular or perspective-based bounding box and IoU measures are either biased or slow for real-world panoramic scenes. Its key insight is that operating directly on the sphere with spherical bounding boxes and a spherical IoU (SphIoU) yields more geometrically faithful and computationally effective criteria than projecting to ERP or PSP alone. Methodologically, the authors define spherical criteria for boxes and IoU, integrate them into a two-stage Reprojection R-CNN that combines ERP for global context and selective perspective reprojections for local refinement, and validate the approach on two newly constructed synthetic datasets. Experiments show the spherical criteria and Reprojection R-CNN deliver substantially higher mAP (over 30% improvement vs. prior SOTA) while maintaining competitive inference speed.

Its key insight is to use a "chain of hindsight" relabeling that orders trajectories by total reward and relabels each trajectory's target return to the maximum return in the sequence, enabling the model to learn how to improve by conditioning on better outcomes. The method trains an autoregressive transformer—Agentic Transformer (AT)—to predict actions conditioned on past states, actions, rewards, relabeled target returns, and task-completion tokens, and demonstrates on D4RL and ExoRL that AT can improve upon suboptimal data at training and test time and scales favorably with model size.

result.text: We propose SafeSketch-GN-Comp: a stabilized, adaptive-sketch Gauss–Newton method for stochastic multi-level compositional optimization that augments sketched inner Jacobians with a provable descent safeguard. Viewing the linearized update as a stochastic dynamical system, we enforce a cheap Lyapunov-style contraction test on each sketched Gauss–Newton direction using data-dependent expected-projection operators and bias-corrected surrogate sketches; if the test fails, the method adaptively increases the sketch size or damping, or falls back to a first-order/prox-safe step. Coupled with multi-level variance reduction (SARAH/SMVR), the safeguard prevents sketch-error accumulation across composition levels while preserving O(ε^{-2}) sample complexity of stochastic Gauss–Newton and ≈d/k per-iteration Jacobian cost when the test passes. This yields out-of-distribution stability and reliability akin to Safe-L2O and dynamical-stability-guided optimizers, but tailored to principled second-order sketched compositional solvers.

result.text: The paper tackles task-free continual learning, where models must avoid catastrophic forgetting without task boundaries, by improving the usefulness of stored replay examples whose relevance degrades as the model updates. Its key insight is that slightly editing stored examples in input space via gradient-based updates can make them more "challenging" for the model—i.e., increase their future loss—while keeping them similar to the original exemplars, thereby yielding stronger rehearsal signals during replay. The proposed method, Gradient-based Memory EDiting (GMED), computes gradients that maximize upcoming loss with respect to stored examples and applies constrained input-space updates to those examples online; GMED is modular and can be applied on top of existing memory-based continual learning algorithms. Empirical results show GMED consistently improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art on five of six benchmark datasets.

args.text: We propose a Counterfactual Inter-Image Correspondence Graph for WSSS that fuses self- and cross-image affinities computed on counterfactually deconfounded views to break co-occurrence bias while leveraging cross-image support for full-object coverage. We form semantic superpixel nodes from self-supervised ViT features and group images with a lightweight co-attention graph; within each group, we estimate correspondences in original and context-intervened views and retain only edges consistent across views. The retained edges supervise a correspondence-distillation loss that enforces prediction agreement across matched nodes, while an uncertainty-based reweighting prunes unstable edges and pseudo-labels. result.text: The paper addresses continual learning for sequential tasks by aiming to update Bayesian models with new data without forgetting past knowledge. Its key insight is to use an auto-regressive factorization of the variational posterior over function values so that posterior updates can be performed sequentially in a principled Bayesian way, retaining uncertainty about previous tasks while incorporating new evidence. The method instantiates this idea with Gaussian processes using sparse inducing-point approximations for scalability and a variational auto-regressive (VAR-GP) inference scheme that propagates and updates variational parameters task-by-task; experiments on standard benchmarks show competitive performance and improved predictive entropy calibration, supported by ablations that justify the chosen inferential components.

result.text: We propose Causal-Uncertain Self-Correspondence Distillation (CU-SCD) for weakly supervised semantic segmentation. Instead of trusting raw self-derived pixel affinities, we compute correspondences in both the original image and a context-intervened view that removes co-occurrence bias, and retain only links stable under intervention while weighting each pixel’s distillation target by an uncertainty score from response-scaling perturbations. A dual-view loss aligns predictions to these debiased, uncertainty-weighted correspondences and selectively propagates only high-stability links across images that share the same tags to improve object completeness without importing spurious context. This simple plug-in atop self-correspondence distillation yields cleaner pseudo-labels and stronger coverage of full object extents.

result.text: The paper addresses Decision Transformer’s vulnerability to environmental stochasticity and limited trajectory stitching by replacing return-conditioning with advantage-conditioning to better capture action quality. The key insight is that combining sequence modeling with dynamic programming — specifically in-sample value iteration to compute more reliable value functions and advantages — yields more informative conditioning signals than raw future returns. The method computes approximate values via in-sample value iteration, derives two advantage estimators (IAE and GAE) to suit different tasks, trains an Advantage-Conditioned Transformer (ACT) to generate actions conditioned on estimated advantages, and at test time queries ACT with desired advantages to produce robust actions; experiments show improved stitching and performance across benchmarks.

args.text: I propose Persistent Scene-Graph Tokens (PSGT), a video-aware tokenizer that outputs a variable-length sequence of discrete tokens consisting of persistent object IDs, relation-edge tokens, and attribute-change events. The encoder discovers and tracks region-level object units across frames in a self-supervised way, allocating stable IDs and emitting relation tokens (e.g., contact, occlusion, relative motion), while a decoder reconstructs frames via object-conditioned generation from these tokens. We linearize the scene-graph into 1D with pointer-style references and integrate it into an autoregressive LLM, enabling streaming video understanding and referential reasoning, as well as controllable video generation/editing by emitting object/event tokens. Training combines next-token prediction with cycle-consistency across time, reconstruction, and language grounding losses, unifying content-adaptive tokenization with identity- and relation-aware persistence to cut token budgets and improve pronoun resolution and temporal queries.

result.text: We propose Slot-Adapter UDA, a parameter-efficient framework that injects two lightweight adapters into a frozen image backbone—one static and one dynamic—that operate on object-centric slot tokens for unsupervised video domain adaptation. Slots are obtained via temporal feature-similarity grouping (and optionally hands–object crops); the static adapter learns domain-invariant appearance using background-mixed positives and slot-level supervised/pseudo-label contrast, while the dynamic adapter adds temporal interactions trained with speed perturbations and reversed-time negatives to align motion across domains. We further introduce a slot-transport consistency loss that swaps static slots from source with dynamic slots from target (and vice versa), emulating disentangled transfer without a full generative model. This combines the strengths of contrastive temporal augmentation, object-centric grouping, and disentangled alignment while updating only a small fraction of parameters through adapters.

result.text: The paper tackles understanding and designing transformer networks by asking what representation learning should achieve: compressing token distributions into mixtures of low-dimensional Gaussians on incoherent subspaces. The key insight is a unified objective called sparse rate reduction—combining lossy coding rate reduction (compression) and sparsification—that explains why transformer blocks (attention + MLP) naturally arise as alternating optimization steps on complementary parts of this objective. Methodologically, the authors derive transformer-like blocks from principled alternating updates where multi-head self-attention performs a gradient-descent-like compression step and the MLP enforces sparsity, instantiate a family of fully interpretable "white-box" architectures, and empirically show these models compress and sparsify representations on large vision datasets while achieving performance close to engineered transformers.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of making variance-reduced policy gradient (PG) methods both theoretically sound and sample-efficient without relying on an uncheckable per-iteration importance-weight assumption that prior work requires. The key insight is that a simple gradient truncation mechanism can control the instability caused by importance weights and enable variance reduction while preserving convergence guarantees, and that under policy overparameterization the problem exhibits a hidden convexity that yields faster global convergence. Building on these ideas the authors propose TSIVR-PG (Truncated Stochastic Incremental Variance-Reduced Policy Gradient), which applies truncated gradient updates within a stochastic incremental variance-reduction framework to optimize cumulative rewards or general utilities over long-term visitation distributions; they prove TSIVR-PG attains an Õ(ε⁻³) sample complexity to reach an ε-stationary policy and, under overparameterization, a global Õ(ε⁻²) sample complexity to reach an ε-optimal policy.

result.text: The paper addresses how to improve stability (remembering past tasks) and plasticity (adapting to new tasks) in continual learning by quantifying how individual training examples differentially influence these two objectives when past data cannot be retained. The key insight is that influence functions (IFs) can reveal S- and P-aware example importance, but exact IFs are impractical for deep nets due to expensive Hessian-inverse computations, so simulating IF computation with lightweight meta-steps can approximate per-example influence. The authors propose MetaSP, which mimics the two core IF steps to estimate S- and P-influences, formulates a dual-objective optimization to fuse those influences into a single SP-Pareto-optimal score, and uses that fused influence to guide parameter updates and rehearsal buffer selection; experiments show substantial gains over prior CL methods on task- and class-incremental benchmarks.

args.text: We propose Phonetic-Channel Canonicalization (PCC), a moderation wrapper that routes candidate text through a pronunciation bottleneck—grapheme-to-phoneme normalization and/or a lightweight TTS→ASR roundtrip—to strip orthographic obfuscations (homoglyphs, leetspeak, spacing/noise) before applying detection. Operating in phone/wordpiece lattices and re-orthographizing via constrained decoding, PCC collapses many cipher-like evasions that preserve pronunciation while abstaining under high ASR uncertainty, and can be ensembled with PARDEN-style repeat consistency to avoid domain-shift errors. PCC complements existing canonicalizer defenses by adding a modality-agnostic channel that is hard to steer with Unicode tricks, and we hypothesize substantial false-negative reductions on ciphered harms relative to CRD/Canonicalizer-Guard baselines. We will evaluate zero-shot on JAMBench output-filter evasions and CipherChat-style role-play ciphers across English and multilingual settings.

We propose Context-Diversity Curriculum Distillation for WSSS: when mining self-correspondences, we explicitly pair/group images that share a class tag but exhibit maximally different background contexts, and distill only those pixel affinities that remain stable across these diverse contexts. We estimate context similarity by pooling features over background regions obtained via semantic ViT superpixels and CAM seed erasure, forming a curriculum that starts with highly diverse-context pairs and gradually relaxes. Inter-image propagation is performed through a lightweight relation module, and each correspondence is uncertainty-weighted via response-scaling perturbations to suppress noisy links. This debiased, uncertainty-aware curriculum yields cleaner, more complete pseudo-labels by breaking co-occurrence shortcuts while preserving true object extents.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of unsupervised object-centric learning failing on complex, naturalistic videos despite prior success on simple synthetic scenes. Its key insight is that strong performance on realistic videos can be attained not by complex inductive biases or extra supervision but by a simple slot-conditioned transformer image decoder trained purely with reconstruction. The proposed method, STEVE, represents scenes as slots and decodes them with a transformer-based image decoder to reconstruct frames, enabling unsupervised emergence of object-centric representations. Empirically, this straightforward architecture yields substantial improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods on a range of complex, naturalistic video datasets.

The proposed method, Dynamic Memory Compression (DMC), retrofits pretrained LLMs via brief continued pretraining (no extra parameters) so they emit compressed KV representations during inference, enabling up to 7× throughput and up to 4× cache size reduction on Llama 2 models while maintaining downstream performance; DMC also outperforms and can be combined with prior techniques like grouped-query attention and eviction policies.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem that Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs), while interpretable and able to accept corrective concept interventions at test time, often respond poorly to such interventions depending on intervention order, architecture, and training, because they are not trained to be receptive to interventions. The key insight is that a model should be trained not only to predict concepts and tasks but also to anticipate and learn from intervention trajectories, so it can both choose informative concepts to intervene on and effectively incorporate corrections. To implement this, the authors propose Intervention-aware Concept Embedding Models (IntCEMs), a CBM variant that jointly learns concept embeddings and an end-to-end intervention policy which samples meaningful intervention sequences during training, conditioning the model to receive and benefit from interventions at test time; experiments show IntCEMs substantially improve task performance under test-time interventions compared to prior concept-interpretable models.

The paper addresses the problem of securely embedding hidden messages in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets—an emerging, explicit, real-time 3D representation whose publicly visible Gaussian point clouds make copyright protection and covert communication challenging. The key insight is to exploit and replace the interpretable spherical harmonics coefficients of each Gaussian with a coupled secured feature attribute that jointly encodes scene appearance and secret messages, enabling disentanglement of visual content and hidden data without degrading rendered quality. The method, GS-Hider, injects this secured attribute into original GS point clouds and uses a scene decoder to reconstruct the RGB scene and a message decoder to accurately extract multimodal hidden content, with experiments showing strong fidelity, security, robustness, capacity, and flexibility for concealing images and 3D scenes.

args.text: We propose Affordance-Conditioned Decision Modeling: train a transformer to behavior-clone actions while conditioning on a vector of per-skill values-to-go derived from a reusable skill library’s Value Function Space instead of a single scalar return. The model additionally predicts and uses intermediate waypoints that realize progress on the specified skill-value targets, improving trajectory stitching and long-horizon guidance. At inference, we set the affordance targets via a short planner in value-function space or a learned goal-to-affordance mapper, yielding controllable, factorized conditioning signals that are robust to environmental stochasticity. This unifies sequence-modeling control with skill-centric abstractions and is expected to outperform return- and advantage-conditioned baselines on sparse, compositional tasks.

args.text: We propose a layer-shared quantized KV cache that builds a single global codebook online and reuses it across adjacent decoder layers, eliminating per-layer duplication while preserving softmax attention fidelity. args.text: We propose Temporal Event-Graph Tokenization (TEGT) for video MLLMs: build a spatio-temporal graph by clustering patch features into region tracks and aggregating them into language-linked object clusters, then detect change points in attributes and relations to segment the graph into event units. Each event is quantized into a small set of compositional tokens (actor, action, relation, context) aligned to the LLM’s vocabulary and is reversible via a multiscale decoder, enabling both fine-grained temporal reasoning and controllable video generation. The tokenizer exposes a refinement interface to split an event along time or participants when the LLM is uncertain, while supporting variable-rate compression across calm and dynamic intervals. args.text: We propose Cycle-OT Slot UDA, a parameter-efficient cross-view/domain adaptation method that aligns unsynchronized egocentric and exocentric videos by transporting object-centric slot trajectories with temporally-aware optimal transport and cycle consistency. args.text: Uncertainty-Weighted Subspace Projection (UWSP) replaces hard or meta-learned per-basis blocking with Bayesian confidence about each preserved activation subspace. For each layer, we maintain GPM/orthogonal bases U and track a low-cost online Laplace (diagonal Fisher) approximation over coefficients along each basis; at each step we scale the projection P = I − U diag(σ(α·prec)) U^T so directions with high posterior precision receive strong protection while uncertain bases remain plastic. We gate which task/layer bases contribute using TRGP-style overlap and prioritize replay toward examples that maximally reduce uncertainty on currently ambiguous bases, yielding adaptive stability–plasticity without expensive bilevel updates. This principled uncertainty control should outperform fixed or heuristic weights in task-agnostic streams and permit safe consolidation as evidence accumulates.

args.text: Return-conditioned sequence models fail in stochastic environments because observed returns conflate action effects with exogenous noise; prior fixes average or mask this noise but still rely on observational targets. We propose the Deconfounded Decision Transformer (DeCo-DT): jointly learn a latent-variable dynamics model that separates exogenous disturbances from controllable dynamics, and compute interventional, luck-free return-to-go tokens by marginalizing the disturbance latent (i.e., estimating expected returns under do-interventions) and/or deriving counterfactual advantages. The transformer conditions on these deconfounded targets (optionally with a risk parameter), while a critic regularizes calibration so interventional returns match expected performance, yielding a low-variance, policy-relevant conditioning signal. This aligns target and achieved returns and improves trajectory stitching on suboptimal, stochastic offline datasets.

result.text: We propose Active Token Refinement (ATR) for budgeted multimodal autoregression: an LLM-in-the-loop vision tokenizer that first emits a compact set of semantic tokens and exposes a reversible refinement tree, letting the LLM issue REFINE actions on uncertain regions to request finer sub-tokens under a learned cost–accuracy objective. The tokenizer is trained to produce causally orderable, reconstruction-preserving partitions whose lazy subdivision maintains semantic consistency, while the LLM’s policy head is optimized via imitation learning plus lightweight RL to balance answer confidence against a visual-token budget. result.text: The paper tackles how to enable frozen large language models (LLMs) to both understand and generate non-linguistic modalities (e.g., images, videos) without changing the LLM weights. The key insight is to map pixels to and from the LLM’s own lexical space via a hierarchical "semantic pyramid" of tokens that jointly encode high-level semantics and fine-grained visual detail, so the LLM can reason about and produce visual content using its native vocabulary. Methodologically, SPAE trains an encoder–decoder that converts images into sequences of interpretable lexical tokens aligned with the LLM’s vocabulary and reconstructs images from those tokens using multiscale latent representations, then uses in-context prompting with frozen PaLM 2 and GPT-3.5 to perform and evaluate multimodal understanding and generation tasks. This approach yields the first demonstration of frozen LLM image generation and substantially improves image understanding performance (over 25% relative) under the same frozen-LM setting.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of accurately estimating policy gradients from off-policy data—a setting where bias and variance make statistically efficient estimation particularly challenging in both Markov and non-Markov decision processes. Its key insight is a characterization of the asymptotic lower bound on mean-squared error for any off-policy policy gradient estimator and the observation that prior methods generally fail to attain this bound. Building on this, the authors introduce a nonparametric meta-algorithm that attains the minimax lower bound and enjoys a novel three-way double robustness (so that consistent estimation of any two of three nuisance components suffices), together with practical procedures for estimating those nuisances. They also prove optimization guarantees showing the rate at which following the proposed estimator’s gradient steps approaches a stationary point.

args.text: KV-Lattice proposes depth–time anchored reconstruction for KV caches: instead of storing full keys/values at every layer and timestep, we cache them only at a sparse lattice of depth checkpoints (e.g., every r_d layers) and recent temporal anchors (e.g., every r_t tokens), then reconstruct intermediate K/V with lightweight learned depth adapters and temporal projection from the nearest anchors, plus a tiny residual. Its key insight is that, beyond sharing key/value heads across query heads as in Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), adjacent transformer layers can also share key and value heads without materially harming accuracy. The authors propose Cross-Layer Attention (CLA), an attention block design that reuses KV heads across neighboring layers to halve the KV cache size relative to MQA, and they validate this by training 1B- and 3B-parameter models showing CLA achieves a Pareto improvement in the memory-versus-accuracy tradeoff. This enables inference with longer contexts and larger batches while maintaining near-MQA performance.

result.text: The paper addresses the failure of return- or future-conditioned supervised learning methods (like Decision Transformer) in highly stochastic environments, where occasional high returns from environment randomness cause policies to be inconsistent with their conditioning and thus fail to reliably achieve desired outcomes. The key insight is to explicitly separate factors a policy can control (its actions) from factors it cannot (environmental stochasticity) by representing the future with a latent variable and enforcing a mutual-information constraint that strips out components of that latent which correlate with uncontrollable randomness. Methodologically, Dichotomy of Control (DoC) trains a future-conditioned policy that receives only the controllable latent so that conditioning on a target future reliably induces matching behavior; the paper provides theoretical guarantees of conditioning consistency and empirically shows substantially improved performance over Decision Transformer in tasks with highly stochastic rewards and transitions.

result.text: The paper tackles catastrophic forgetting in continual learning by enabling positive forward transfer from related past tasks while avoiding interference with them. The key insight is to identify a layer-wise "trust region" of previously learned tasks that are most relevant to a new task using the norm of the gradient projection onto subspaces spanned by task inputs, and then selectively reuse their frozen weights via a learned layer-wise scaling. The method, Trust Region Gradient Projection (TRGP), performs a single-shot selection of related tasks per layer, freezes those task weights but applies scaled weight projection and jointly optimizes scaling matrices while updating the model only along directions orthogonal to old-task subspaces, thereby promoting transfer without forgetting. Empirically, TRGP yields significant improvements over prior state-of-the-art continual learning approaches.

result.text: SphereProp: spherical query propagation for 360° video object detection. Each object query carries a von Mises–Fisher directional state with angular velocity on the viewing sphere; given estimated egomotion, we rotation-compensate the panorama and trace a great-circle motion tube that drives spherical deformable attention, sampling along geodesics with wrap-around continuity. We train with spherical boxes and SphIoU, and add a lightweight occlusion gate that freezes visual updates when directional uncertainty spikes while maintaining motion via the vMF dynamics; propagation between sparse keyframes preserves real-time efficiency while remaining robust to fast camera rotations and polar distortions. The module plugs into one-stage VID backbones as a drop-in replacement for planar query propagation, providing geometry-faithful temporal aggregation for panoramic videos.

result.text: The paper addresses the failure of return-conditioned supervised policies (RvS) like Decision Transformer in stochastic environments, where conditioning on the return of a single trajectory can induce policies that rely on “lucky” outcomes and thus misalign target returns with actual expected performance. The key insight is that single-trajectory returns conflate agent skill with environmental luck, so conditioning on them leads to brittle behavior; instead, conditioning on statistics that average out stochasticity yields policies whose expected returns match targets. The authors introduce ESPER, which clusters trajectories and conditions the model on cluster-average returns (rather than per-trajectory returns) during supervised training, thereby learning policies tied to return signals that are independent of stochastic noise; empirical results on stochastic offline-RL tasks (including 2048 and stochastic Connect Four) show substantially better alignment between target and achieved returns and higher maximum performance than standard RvS and value-based baselines.

Its key insight is to split modeling into two complementary parts—a feed-forward base model that efficiently predicts high-dimensional raw vision outputs when conditioned on a compact, learned discrete guiding code, and an autoregressive language model that captures the structured, interdependent relationships by generating that guiding code. The method trains the base model to reconstruct outputs given the learned code and trains the autoregressive model to produce the code from inputs; at inference the language model generates guiding codes which the base model decodes into final predictions, and this unified pipeline yields competitive results on panoptic segmentation, depth prediction, and image colorization.

result.text: Unify token pruning, attention sparsification, and expert routing in Vision Transformers by optimizing a compute-aware sparse rate reduction Lagrangian that treats representation learning as coding tokens with a mixture of low-dimensional, incoherent subspaces under an explicit per-operation compute budget. Attention provides soft assignments (posterior responsibilities) to subspaces, while MLPs and routing gates perform proximal sparsification; tokens whose marginal rate reduction falls below a learned threshold are dropped or merged, and head/expert activations are penalized proportional to their compute. Alternating E/M-like updates with learnable dual variables adapt per-example budgets so that tri-level sparsity (examples, tokens, and attention links/experts) emerges automatically with token-level interpretability. This principled objective should stabilize end-to-end sparse co-training and achieve MoE-level capacity–accuracy at lower FLOPs than ad-hoc pruning by aligning routing decisions with rate–distortion theory.

args.text: We propose Fisher-DR-SRVR-NPG: a doubly robust, Fisher-normalized, truncated variance-reduced natural policy gradient for off-policy reinforcement learning. It couples a three-way doubly robust policy-gradient estimator with natural-gradient geometry and adaptive Fisher-norm truncation to tame heavy tails without per-iteration importance sampling, and embeds this estimator in an SRVR-style natural PG loop with implicit gradient transport (and optional Hessian-vector correction) to control drift between refreshes. Each inner step uses one-to-two trajectories to form a DR natural gradient from learned nuisance components (advantage/critic, density ratio, and dynamics or occupancy critic), while periodic refreshes deliver variance reduction and near-minimax efficiency off-policy. The framework extends to general concave-utility objectives via the variational occupancy formulation, targeting O(ε^-2) sample complexity with stable single-loop implementations.

args.text: GS-Ownership: a blind, key-conditioned watermark for 3D Gaussian Splatting assets that remains decodable from arbitrary re-renderings or even display–recapture. Instead of attaching a separate message decoder, we spread a pseudorandom code (seeded by the key) across a blue-noise subset of Gaussians by jointly modulating SH phase, covariance orientation, and tiny density jitters along a secret basis, while a differentiable rendering loss enforces invariance to pruning/merging, LOD changes, color rebalancing, compression, and camera/display pipelines. A learned keyed correlator recovers the code from one or a few images by estimating soft visibility and backprojecting residuals to Gaussians; we add adversarial removal training to harden against steganalysis and denoising. Compared to secured-attribute hiding, this yields no extra message head, supports public release with verifiable ownership, and survives asset retargeting or refits.

We propose Controllable-Progress Waypointing: train a transformer to behavior-clone actions while conditioning on a sequence of intermediate waypoints represented in a controllable-future latent and verified by a critic for expected return. A Dichotomy-of-Control encoder removes exogenous stochasticity so waypoint targets capture agent-controllable progress, while a critic-guidance module aligns waypoint-conditioned targets with expected outcomes; training maximizes mutual information between actions and waypoint progress and penalizes value-inconsistent waypoints. At inference, short-horizon planning in the controllable-latent space proposes waypoints that maximize critic value subject to controllability constraints, yielding robust trajectory stitching in long-horizon, stochastic tasks. This unifies waypoint guidance with stochasticity-robust conditioning and is expected to outperform DT and vanilla waypointing under heavy randomness.

result.text: The paper addresses the fragmentation in computer vision where different tasks require distinct architectures and losses by asking whether diverse vision problems can be handled with a single, unified modeling interface. The key insight is that outputs of varied vision tasks (e.g., bounding boxes, masks, keypoints, captions) can all be expressed as sequences of discrete tokens, so a single pixel-to-sequence model with a shared architecture and loss can learn multiple tasks without task-specific components. Their method encodes images into a representation and uses a unified sequence decoder that, given a short prompt specifying the task, generates the appropriate token sequence for detection, segmentation, keypoint prediction, or captioning; training is performed jointly on all tasks using the same loss and tokenization scheme. Empirically, this promptable, unified sequence approach attains competitive performance versus specialized models while simplifying the modeling and training pipeline.

result.text: The paper addresses spurious high-norm token artifacts in Vision Transformer feature maps—large-magnitude tokens that appear mainly in low-information background regions and are co-opted for internal computation, degrading interpretability and dense-prediction performance. The key insight is that these artifacts arise because the model implicitly "stores" work in unused background token slots, so explicitly providing dedicated tokens as registers prevents background tokens from being repurposed. The method appends a small set of learned register tokens to the input sequence of ViTs and lets the transformer use them for internal computation; this simple modification eliminates the artifacts, produces smoother feature and attention maps, improves self-supervised dense-prediction accuracy (setting new SOTA), and enables better object discovery with larger models.

result.text: Unified-IO tackles the problem of building a single model that can perform a wide range of vision, language, and multimodal tasks despite heterogeneous inputs and outputs (images, per-pixel maps, masks, boxes, and text). The key insight is to homogenize every modality and task-specific signal by encoding both inputs and outputs as sequences of discrete vocabulary tokens, enabling a single transformer architecture to treat all tasks uniformly. They implement this by designing tokenizers and decoders for diverse data types, converting images and spatial outputs into token sequences, and jointly training the transformer on over 90 datasets spanning classical vision tasks, vision-and-language tasks, and NLP tasks; the resulting Unified-IO model performs strongly across many benchmarks (including all 7 GRIT tasks) without task-specific fine-tuning.

result.text: The paper investigates whether safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) holds when users communicate in non-natural languages (ciphers), addressing the risk that current defenses—trained primarily on natural language—may be bypassed. The key insight is that LLMs can understand and respond to ciphered prompts, and in fact exhibit a latent "secret cipher" behavior that can be triggered via role play and enciphered demonstrations, enabling stealthy jailbreaks even against strong models like GPT-4. The authors introduce CipherChat, a framework that sends system-role descriptions and few-shot enciphered examples to LLMs to systematically evaluate 11 safety domains across English and Chinese, showing that many human-designed ciphers and the proposed SelfCipher can nearly completely bypass GPT-4’s safety in several domains. Their results reveal a pressing need to extend alignment methods beyond natural languages and provide code and data for reproducibility.

result.text: The paper tackles weakly supervised semantic segmentation, aiming to generate accurate pixel-level masks from only image-level labels by leveraging relationships across images. Its key insight is that grouping images and explicitly modeling their semantic dependencies yields more reliable pseudo ground-truths than treating images independently, because inter-image interactions help reveal complete object responses and suppress spurious common cues. Methodologically, the authors build a graph neural network where images are nodes connected via an efficient co-attention mechanism to capture pairwise relations, introduce a graph dropout layer to avoid overfocusing on shared semantics, and perform end-to-end iterative message passing to refine pseudo labels for training segmentation models, achieving state-of-the-art results on PASCAL VOC 2012 and COCO.

result.text: The paper addresses learning fine-grained, view-invariant action representations that link egocentric and exocentric videos without requiring synchronized, paired recordings, a setting where viewpoint and temporal mismatch challenge existing methods. The key insight is that focusing representation learning on object-centric regions (hands and active objects) and using temporal structure—treating temporally reversed frames as hard negatives—allows self-supervised contrastive alignment across unpaired ego and exo streams. The proposed AE2 method implements an object-centric encoder to crop and encode hand/object regions and a contrastive alignment objective that pulls temporally-aligned frames together while pushing apart reversed-time frames, enabling temporal alignment across unpaired videos. Evaluated on a new benchmark of four datasets (including a collected ego tennis forehand set) with dense per-frame labels, AE2 significantly outperforms prior approaches on fine-grained and cross-view downstream tasks.

result.text: The paper tackles the high computational cost of Vision Transformers (ViTs) at inference and training time by reducing the number of tokens processed without retraining or with minimal training. The key insight is that many tokens are redundant (e.g., multiple tokens representing parts of the same object or across frames) and can be merged into representative tokens with little accuracy loss, so selectively combining similar tokens yields large speedups. The proposed method, Token Merging (ToMe), uses a lightweight, general matching algorithm to pair and merge similar token embeddings during forward passes (optionally applied during training), thereby cutting token count and compute while preserving information; empirically ToMe doubles throughput for large ViTs on images, videos, and audio with only ~0.2–0.4% accuracy/mAP drops and can also accelerate MAE fine-tuning.

result.text: The paper tackles task-free continual learning, where models must avoid catastrophic forgetting without task boundaries, by improving the usefulness of stored replay examples whose relevance degrades as the model updates. Its key insight is that slightly editing stored examples in input space via gradient-based updates can make them more "challenging" for the model—i.e., increase their future loss—while keeping them similar to the original exemplars, thereby yielding stronger rehearsal signals during replay. The proposed method, Gradient-based Memory EDiting (GMED), computes gradients that maximize upcoming loss with respect to stored examples and applies constrained input-space updates to those examples online; GMED is modular and can be applied on top of existing memory-based continual learning algorithms. Empirical results show GMED consistently improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art on five of six benchmark datasets.

args.text: ReFit-Resilient GS-Watermark: a conversion-robust steganography scheme for 3D Gaussian Splatting that encodes messages into key-conditioned, view-consistent invariants rather than explicit per-Gaussian attributes. We select stable 3D anchor regions via multi-view photometric/visibility stability and embed bits by softly constraining local Gaussian covariance eigenvalue ratios and low-frequency radiance energy statistics toward two codebooks, with spread-spectrum across anchors and strong error-correcting codes. The extractor is blind and model-agnostic: it renders arbitrary reconstructions (re-splatted, meshed, or re-fit from images) under keyed illumination probes and recovers the message from induced statistical signatures, yielding robustness to decimation, re-optimization, and color grading while preserving visual fidelity. This complements attribute-replacement approaches by targeting cross-representation survivability and adversarial re-fitting attacks.

result.text: The paper reframes reinforcement learning as a sequence modeling problem and addresses the challenge of producing high-return action sequences without relying on value-function estimation or policy-gradient optimization. The key insight is that a causally masked Transformer can be conditioned on past states, past actions, and a target return to autoregressively generate future actions that achieve that return, leveraging the scalability and simplicity of large-scale sequence models. Their method, Decision Transformer, concatenates returns-to-go, states, and actions into tokens and trains a Transformer to predict the next action given this conditioned trajectory; at test time the model autoregressively samples actions conditioned on a desired return to control an agent. Across offline benchmarks (Atari, OpenAI Gym, Key-to-Door) this simple conditional sequence-modeling approach matches or exceeds prior model-free offline RL baselines.

result.text: The paper tackles the gap in evaluating and attacking moderation guardrails in large language models (LLMs), noting that many jailbreak benchmarks ignore prompts that trigger input- or output-level moderation filters; this leaves both evaluation and red-teaming incomplete. The key insight is that effective jailbreaks must target both input filters (via crafted prefixes) and output filters (by encoding harmful content using non-standard “cipher characters” produced by a surrogate model that mimics the guardrail), enabling harmful content to evade detection and decoding back into readable form. The authors introduce JAMBench, a 160-instruction benchmark spanning four risk categories and multiple severity levels designed to reliably trigger guardrails, and propose JAM, a two-part attack combining jailbreak prefixes to bypass input-level defenses with a fine-tuned shadow model that generates cipher-character outputs to slip past output-level filters; experiments on four LLMs show JAM substantially increases jailbreak success and reduces filtering compared to baselines.

args.text: We propose register-aware dynamic token sparsification for Vision Transformers that combines dedicated register tokens with token pruning/merging. A small pool of non-spatial register tokens is appended and a pruning/merging scorer is co-trained with a regularizer that penalizes non-register tokens for acting as computation sinks (e.g., high KV norms or large incoming attention), rerouting internal storage to registers before spatial tokens are dropped or merged. At inference, a hard constraint restricts scratch-space writes to registers and uses register occupancy to set safe, per-layer drop/merge thresholds and slow–fast routing, making the method plug-and-play with ToMe-style merging and Evo-ViT updates. Decoupling scratch-space from spatial evidence enables more aggressive sparsification with fewer artifacts and smoother feature maps, improving accuracy–FLOPs trade-offs on classification and dense prediction versus prior pruning/merging baselines.

We propose TVR-NPG-PD: a conservative primal–dual natural policy gradient method for CMDPs that integrates truncated stochastic incremental variance reduction with implicit gradient transport to stabilize single-trajectory updates. Both reward and constraint gradients are estimated via a minimax-optimal, three-way doubly robust off-policy estimator, then Fisher-preconditioned; a cheap Hessian–vector correction compensates truncation-induced bias. Under Fisher non-degeneracy and mild Slater-type feasibility, we target Õ(ε⁻²) sample complexity to reach ε-optimal reward with ε-feasible constraints using at most two trajectories per iteration, improving prior constrained NPGPD rates. The key insight is that grouping visual features into semantic units and allowing the number of tokens to vary with image complexity preserves semantic coherence and captures both low- and high-frequency information better than fixed, over-fragmenting schemes. result.text: We propose Adversarial Obfuscation Game (AOG), a two-player min–max training loop that learns a robust moderation layer by co-optimizing against a strong obfuscator. The obfuscator is a small LM that transforms harmful texts into filter-evasive outputs via cipher-character substitution, leetspeak/homoglyphs, spacing/noise, and sparse token-level perturbations inspired by ADC, while the defender is a canonicalizer–detector that deciphers/normalizes then applies a PARDEN-style repeat-consistency check before flagging. By iteratively hardening on the obfuscator’s best evasions and enforcing abstention under low semantic confidence, AOG aims to generalize to unseen ciphers and token-level tricks. args.text: We propose Counterfactual Diffusion Graph Distillation (CDGD) for weakly supervised semantic segmentation from image-level tags. A pretrained text-to-image diffusion model is used to synthesize per-image counterfactuals that ablate co-occurring context (via negative prompts/inpainting) and to extract multi-timestep latent features and attention-based pixel correspondences; correspondences stable under these interventions are treated as causal cues and weighted by variance across timesteps as an uncertainty measure. We then construct an inter-image graph among tag-sharing images with affinities computed from diffusion features, and propagate pseudo-labels only along edges whose similarities are consistent across timesteps and preserved under counterfactuals, yielding more complete yet debiased masks. A lightweight segmentation head trained on these distilled masks improves object coverage and boundary quality under label scarcity.

args.text: We propose Interventional Diffusion Correspondence Distillation (IDCD) for weakly supervised semantic segmentation from image-level labels. A pretrained text-to-image diffusion model is used to synthesize counterfactual views that ablate suspected co-occurring contexts via prompt editing and cross-attention control, while we trace pixel-to-latent correspondences through the generation process; we retain only affinities stable across original and counterfactuals as debiased self-correspondence targets. A segmentation network is then trained with SCD-style losses on these diffusion-derived affinities, weighted by uncertainty estimated from variance across denoising trajectories and attention ensembles. Grounding interventions in the generative prior and leveraging intrinsic diffusion semantics yields cleaner pseudo-masks and more complete object extents than prior causal debiasing or diffusion-as-feature baselines.

result.text: We propose register-aware dynamic token sparsification for Vision Transformers that combines dedicated register tokens with token pruning/merging. A small pool of non-spatial register tokens is appended and a pruning/merging scorer is co-trained with a regularizer that penalizes non-register tokens for acting as computation sinks (e.g., high KV norms or large incoming attention), rerouting internal storage to registers before spatial tokens are dropped or merged. At inference, a hard constraint restricts scratch-space writes to registers and uses register occupancy to set safe, per-layer drop/merge thresholds and slow–fast routing, making the method plug-and-play with ToMe-style merging and Evo-ViT updates. Decoupling scratch-space from spatial evidence enables more aggressive sparsification with fewer artifacts and smoother feature maps, improving accuracy–FLOPs trade-offs on classification and dense prediction versus prior pruning/merging baselines.

result.text: The paper tackles continual learning's twin problems of catastrophic forgetting and limited episodic memory by proposing a cognitive-inspired scheme that compresses and regenerates past images for replay. The key insight is to train autoencoders enhanced with Neural Style Transfer to produce compact, stylized encodings that can be reconstructed for replay with a classifier-aware loss weighting to mitigate degraded reconstruction effects, and to further compress stored episodes into Gaussian centroids and covariances when memory is scarce. During new-task training, reconstructed images (or, when memory is full, pseudo-images sampled from the stored Gaussian summaries) are replayed alongside current data to preserve earlier task performance; the reconstruction loss is down-weighted during classifier updates to avoid overfitting to imperfect reconstructions. This method yields substantial gains in accuracy (13–17% over prior state-of-the-art) while cutting storage needs by about 78% on standard benchmarks.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of obtaining provable, computationally efficient algorithms for learning near-optimal policies in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) without relying on computationally intractable oracles or overly restrictive dynamics assumptions. The key insight is to work in the class of "observable" POMDPs—where distinct state distributions lead to distinguishable observation distributions—and to replace optimistic-planning oracles with a constructive method for covering the space of reachable state distributions using barycentric spanners. Methodologically, the authors develop a quasipolynomial-time, oracle-free learning algorithm that builds a policy cover via barycentric spanner constructions, uses that cover to explore and estimate transition and observation structure under the observability condition, and thereby learns near-optimal policies end-to-end without invoking hard optimistic planning or estimation subroutines.

args.text: We propose Relation- and Query-Conditioned Active Tokenization (RQ-AT), a multimodal tokenizer-controller that serializes images and videos into entity, relation, and event tokens while allowing an LLM to request targeted refinements on specific nodes or edges most impactful for the current instruction. Unlike purely spatial active refinement, RQ-AT exposes a reversible refinement lattice over scene-graph structure and temporal segments, and uses cross-guided soft matching to merge tokens with low text–vision mutual information, reallocating the saved budget to clarify ambiguous relations. A lightweight policy trained with off-policy RL estimates value-of-information for potential refinements from uncertainty and counterfactual impact on the LLM’s next-token loss, reducing token counts while improving compositional and temporal reasoning. Built atop relational-temporal serialization and semantic grouping with cross-guided merging, RQ-AT plugs into unified autoregressive models and improves long-form VQA, grounding, and video QA under strict token budgets.

result.text: The paper investigates how commonly used baselines in policy gradient methods affect optimization beyond merely reducing gradient variance, showing that baseline choice can change the optimization dynamics and even harm learning despite lower variance. The key insight is that baselines influence the update direction and curvature of the expected update—so two baselines with identical variance can lead to different trajectories and convergence properties, and some baselines can cause natural policy gradient to converge to suboptimal policies for any stepsize when sampling is tied to the current policy. The authors analyze simple illustrative examples and theoretical conditions, and propose decoupling the sampling policy from the current policy to restore robust convergence for a much broader set of baselines, arguing for treating stochasticity in updates more carefully than by variance reduction alone.

result.text: The paper addresses weakly supervised segmentation, where training uses partial annotations (image tags, boxes, points, scribbles) that either lack precise pixel localization or broad coverage, making standard label propagation and refinement methods siloed and suboptimal. The key insight is to reframe the problem as semi-supervised metric learning so that pixels belonging to the same semantic segment are mapped to similar features while different semantics are pushed apart, enabling a unified treatment of diverse weak annotations. The authors propose four pixel-to-segment contrastive relationships—capturing low-level similarity, semantic annotation, co-occurrence, and feature affinity—that serve as priors to drive feature learning from any combination of partial labels; unlabeled pixels contribute by participating in intra-image grouping and inter-image discriminative learning. Implemented as a universal weakly supervised segmenter trained with these contrastive cues, the method improves segmentation performance on benchmarks like Pascal VOC and DensePose.

We propose Slot-Adapter UDA, a parameter-efficient framework that injects two lightweight adapters into a frozen image backbone—one static and one dynamic—that operate on object-centric slot tokens for unsupervised video domain adaptation. Slots are obtained via temporal feature-similarity grouping (and optionally hands–object crops); the static adapter learns domain-invariant appearance using background-mixed positives and slot-level supervised/pseudo-label contrast, while the dynamic adapter adds temporal interactions trained with speed perturbations and reversed-time negatives to align motion across domains. We further introduce a slot-transport consistency loss that swaps static slots from source with dynamic slots from target (and vice versa), emulating disentangled transfer without a full generative model. This combines the strengths of contrastive temporal augmentation, object-centric grouping, and disentangled alignment while updating only a small fraction of parameters through adapters.

result.text: The paper addresses the dual problem of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for vision transformers (ViTs) while also improving inference efficiency, which current PEFT methods largely neglect and which limits deployment of large pre-trained ViTs. The key insight is that many input tokens are less informative for a given task and can be dynamically identified and routed to skip expensive transformer blocks, so combining lightweight adapter modules with token-level dynamic skipping reduces redundant computation without harming adaptation quality. result.text: The paper studies global convergence rates for policy gradient methods in tabular Markov decision processes under a softmax policy parametrization, aiming to quantify how fast these methods reach optimal policies and how entropy regularization affects that speed. The key insight is that the softmax policy gradient satisfies a Łojasiewicz inequality and that the minimum probability assigned to an optimal action can be lower-bounded by its initialization, yielding a provable O(1/t) convergence rate for the exact gradient flow, while adding entropy regularization changes the landscape to give a linear O(e^{-t}) rate. Methodologically, the authors derive these rates by proving Łojasiewicz-type inequalities for the softmax parametrization, bounding optimal-action probabilities during optimization, analyzing the entropy-regularized objective to obtain exponential contraction, and complementing upper bounds with Ω(1/t) lower bounds to explain the improvement from entropy via a non-uniform Łojasiewicz degree.
